title: Jam session with Blue Devils members in Oklahoma City, 1932
summary: On the Tiny Taylor tour Phillips and Clifford MacTear jam with Lester and Leroy White in Lester's room; Phillips says Lester's style never changed and he had always been fast.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. See, Kansas City was the Blue Devils' headquarters. See, when we was on this little tour with Tiny, the Blue Devils were playing down in Oklahoma City at a place called the Ritz Ballroom. Bands would go down there and play all the winter.
Phillips - 109
Where Tiny Taylor took the band?
When Tiny took us on this little tour. We run up on Les and them in Oklahoma City.
The Ritz Ballroom.
Yeah, playing the Ritz Ballroom. That's where the Blue Devils was playing. So we met them there, had a little jam session. Leroy White...
He was playing trumpet.
Yeah. We all knew each other from Kansas City.
So you're talking about a session there. And what happened?
Yeah, we had a little session.
Some members of the Blue Devils?
Yeah. Clifford MacTear, who was a hell of a guitar player.
He was King Oliver's guitar player?
Yeah, and Tiny too, because see, that's the same band Bronson had then.
You mentioned Bronson's personnel, but you didn't get into mentioning the personnel as exactly as it was with King Oliver. You just said that Bronson lost the band to King Oliver.
Well, the whole band went with King Oliver.
Phillips - 110
What was the session...?
We went back to Lester's house, played in his room. Cliff played the guitar. He and Roy was living together -Leroy, we called him Roy. And then Roy got his horn out...
Roy was living with Lester?
Roy and Lester was living in the same place.
What about his wife? Where was his wife living?
She was there. Roy's wife, too. The kid, too.
Whose kid was that?
Roy's kid. He had a little boy. He plays on the Yankees ball team now -- Roy White.
That's interesting. Leroy White is the father of Roy White.
Yeah. You've heard of Roy White.
He's not on the Yankees now.
No. He's over in Japan.
He played for a long time.
Well, that's his son. He was a little baby then.
I thought Roy White got born around the late 1930's. Maybe even after 1940. Because he didn't come up into the Major Leagues until around 1966 or 1967.
Phillips - 111
This was in the 1930's... Maybe this is... I guess it's the same one. It should be. He should be around 40-some-years old now.
Anyway, you were talking about this session. You had MacTear and White and you and Lester.
That was all.
So just one guitar and all horns.
Yeah. We was in a room. You can play like that, too, you know. The guitar gets about like a piano if you've got a good one.
So you guys jammed.
Yeah, we jammed.
What kind of ideas was Lester into at that time? Was his style changing any from you had remembered last time, when you played with him with Bronson?

His style ain't never changed! He played the same style he played when he was 14. See what I mean? He ain't changed. And he said he wasn't gonna change. He said he wasn't going to change to the way Fletcher Henderson's wife wanted him to play. He said he didn't like that kind of horn. He said it was all right...
I didn't mean changing in general. I just meant, like, little slight changes. Late in his career he had little slight changes that you can tell. I don't mean trying to copy anybody, but...
Phillips - 112
I mean, he probably added more to it. You know what I mean? He played more than what he was...
That's what I mean. What kind of changes.
As he went on, he played more.
Right. So what was going on at this time? What was he adding on to his style at that time?
I don't know. Maybe faster. Because he always was fast. But when he played "Clap Hands, Here Comes Charlie," that's when I knew he was fast. You ever hear that record?
Yeah, with Basie.
Yeah, real fast.
So that jam session was in 1933.
'32. See, then they left there, and they went to Kansas City.
That was in Kansas City, wasn't it?
That jam session?
That's when they were playing at the Ritz Ballroom.
No, that was in Oklahoma City. They stayed down there all winter. They went down there, like, in November, and they stayed... The ballroom stayed open until around June. People dance, you know.
That's the Ritz Ballroom in Oklahoma City.
Yeah. They closed up in the summer-time. Everything in those days closed up in the summer-time because
Phillips - 113
they didn't have no air-conditioning.
